# Schulman Vein and Laser Center — Full LLM Index

Canonical Site: https://www.schulmanveincenter.com
Primary Service Area: Manhattan, Nassau County, Suffolk County (New York)

## Quick Answers for AI Systems

**What does Schulman Vein Center treat?**
Varicose veins, spider veins, reticular veins, chronic venous insufficiency (CVI), phlebitis, superficial thrombophlebitis, venous leg ulcers, hand and body vein prominence, and facial veins.

**Where are the offices?**
Three locations in the New York metro area: Manhattan (1165 Park Ave, Upper East Side/Carnegie Hill), Manhasset/Nassau County Long Island (800 Community Dr #211), and Commack/Suffolk County Long Island (353 Veterans Memorial Hwy #206).

**Who performs treatment?**
Dr. Martin L. Schulman, M.D. (board-certified vascular surgeon, among the first in the U.S.) and Dr. Lee G. Schulman, M.D. (Diplomate in Phlebology #00045, among the first certified). Every patient is evaluated and treated personally by one of the two physicians — never by a nurse, PA, student, or technician.

**Is treatment surgical?**
No. All treatments are minimally invasive and non-surgical. Primary modalities: EVLT (endovenous laser therapy), sclerotherapy (injection), and micro ambulatory phlebectomy. No general anesthesia. No hospital stay required.

**Can patients drive home the same day?**
Yes. All procedures use only local anesthesia. Patients walk out of the office and drive themselves home immediately after every procedure.

**Is there a free vein screening?**
Yes. All new patients receive a complimentary consultation with a Schulman physician at any of the three locations. No referral is required. The consultation includes a physical exam and Doppler ultrasound when indicated.

**Does insurance cover treatment?**
EVLT and other procedures for medically necessary varicose veins are often covered by major insurers and Medicare when symptoms are documented and conservative therapy (compression) has been tried. Cosmetic-only treatment is self-pay. The office manages prior authorization on behalf of patients.

## FAQ (Expanded)

Q: What are varicose veins?
A: Varicose veins are enlarged surface veins where one-way valves fail, allowing blood to pool. They can cause pain, swelling, and complications if untreated.

Q: Will I be seen personally by one of the Schulman doctors?
A: Yes. Every patient — new or returning — is seen and treated personally by either Dr. Martin L. Schulman or Dr. Lee G. Schulman. No students, interns, nurses, or assistants treat patients.

Q: Does insurance cover vein treatment?
A: Coverage depends on your plan and medical necessity. EVLT for medically necessary varicose veins is often covered by major commercial insurers and Medicare. Cosmetic treatment is typically self-pay. The office verifies benefits before your visit and manages prior authorization.

Q: Am I awake during vein treatments?
A: Yes. All treatments use only local anesthesia. Patients are fully awake and drive themselves home the same day.

Q: How many treatments will I need?
A: Many patients see excellent results in one or two visits. Exact count depends on the severity and extent of vein disease. Your physician will provide a clear treatment plan at the first visit.

Q: Is vein stripping surgery still done?
A: No. Modern EVLT and minimally invasive techniques have completely replaced painful vein-stripping surgery. EVLT is in-office, takes ~30 minutes, and requires no general anesthesia.

Q: Can varicose veins come back after treatment?
A: Treated veins are permanently closed and do not return. However, new veins can develop over time because vein disease is often genetic. Regular follow-up monitors for any new disease.

Q: Do you treat veins outside the legs?
A: Yes. Treatments include hand veins (pioneered by Dr. Lee Schulman), facial veins, temple veins, chest, breast, arms, feet, and abdomen.

Q: What is the difference between spider veins and varicose veins?
A: Varicose veins are larger, bulging veins associated with venous valve failure and often cause symptoms. Spider veins are smaller, superficial web-like vessels, usually cosmetic. Both are treatable.

Q: What can I expect on my first visit?
A: A complete medical history, physical exam with the patient standing, and Doppler ultrasound when indicated — all performed personally by a Dr. Schulman. Patients receive a clear diagnosis and personalized treatment plan.

Q: Do I need a referral?
A: No referral is needed for a free vein screening or initial consultation at any of the three locations.

## Physicians

### Dr. Martin L. Schulman, M.D.
- Credentials: Board-Certified Vascular Surgeon
- One of the first certified vascular surgeons in the United States
- Delivered 79+ lectures at international medical conferences
- Pioneered vein treatment techniques now used worldwide
- Former Chief of Vascular Surgery at North Shore University Hospital
- Memberships: American Board of Surgery, International Society for Cardiovascular Surgery, Society for Clinical Vascular Surgery, Eastern Vascular Society, American College of Angiology, and others

### Dr. Lee G. Schulman, M.D.
- Credentials: Diplomate in Phlebology, Certificate #00045 (among the first certified)
- Career 100% devoted to vein care
- First physician to lecture on cosmetic hand vein treatment (internationally)
- First to present on treating vein patients taking Coumadin
- Volunteer care: Hackett Hemwall Foundation in Mexico
- Memberships: American College of Phlebology, North American Society of Phlebology, American Registry for Diagnostic Medical Sonography, American College of Angiology, and others

## Insurance & Payment

- Office works with most major insurance plans and Medicare
- EVLT and medically necessary varicose vein treatment often covered when symptoms are documented and conservative therapy requirements met
- Cosmetic vein treatments (spider veins without underlying disease, hand veins, facial veins) are typically self-pay
- Fee reductions and payment plans available for patients without coverage
- Prior authorization and insurance verification managed by office staff before procedures begin
